The cardinality of a finite set is the number of elements contained within it. A set is infinite if it has infinitely many elements.

- The set $A$ is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{x-1} \\ {f}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x-1})={e}^{x-1} \\ {f}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x-1})={e}^{x-1} \\ {f}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x-1})={e}^{x-1} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $A$ contains only one element:

$$
A={{e}^{x-1}}.
$$

Consequently, $|A|=1,$ which is finite.

- The set $B$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{-2x} \\ {g}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{-2x})=-2{e}^{-2x} \\ {g}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{e}^{-2x})=4{e}^{-2x} \\ {g}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{-2x})=-8{e}^{-2x} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
B={{e}^{-2x},-2{e}^{-2x},4{e}^{-2x},-8{e}^{-2x},…}
$$

Consequently, $B$ is infinite.

- The set $C$ is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{(0)}(x) & ={e}^{x/2} \\ {h}^{(1)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x/2})=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x/2} \\ {h}^{(2)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x/2})=\frac{1}{4}{e}^{x/2} \\ {h}^{(3)}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{4}{e}^{x/2})=\frac{1}{8}{e}^{x/2} \\ ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we can write our set as follows:

$$
C={{e}^{x/2},\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x/2},\frac{1}{4}{e}^{x/2},\frac{1}{8}{e}^{x/2},…}
$$

Consequently, $C$ is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ and $C$ only."

  • The set A is finite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: f(0)(x)=ex−1f(1)(x)=ddx(ex−1)=ex−1f(2)(x)=ddx(ex−1)=ex−1f(3)(x)=ddx(ex−1)=ex−1⋮ Thus, A contains only one element: A={ex−1}. Consequently, |A|=1, which is finite.

  • The set B is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: g(0)(x)=e−2xg(1)(x)=ddx(e−2x)=−2e−2xg(2)(x)=ddx(−2e−2x)=4e−2xg(3)(x)=ddx(4e−2x)=−8e−2x⋮ Thus, we can write our set as follows: B={e−2x,−2e−2x,4e−2x,−8e−2x,…} Consequently, B is infinite.

  • The set C is infinite. Listing the first few elements of our set, we have the following: h(0)(x)=ex/2h(1)(x)=ddx(ex/2)=12ex/2h(2)(x)=ddx(12ex/2)=14ex/2h(3)(x)=ddx(14ex/2)=18ex/2⋮ Thus, we can write our set as follows: C={ex/2,12ex/2,14ex/2,18ex/2,…} Consequently, C is infinite.

Therefore, the correct answer is "B and C only."
